{"hits": {"hits": [{"created": "2026-10-04T12:20:12.249361+00:00", "modified": "2026-10-04T12:34:51.350610+00:00", "id": 23136727, "conceptrecid": "23136726", "doi": "10.5281/zenodo.23136727", "conceptdoi": "10.5281/zenodo.23136726", "doi_url": "https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23136727", "metadata": {"title": "Open-source data generator for joint ATFCM benchmark instances, v2.0.0", "doi": "10.5281/zenodo.23136727", "publication_date": "2026-10-01", "description": "

Open-source data generator for joint Air Traffic Flow and Capacity Management (ATFCM) benchmark instances, version 2.0.0. From a real flight list of the OpenSky Network it generates solver-ready instances in which flights can be delayed or rerouted and airspace sectors reconfigured so that no sector exceeds its capacity: a navigation graph, sectors with capacities and their allocation, airports, aircraft and filed flights for one 24-hour day.

The pipeline has six stages: the demand model (per-airport departure profiles, an origin- and time-conditional destination model, flight durations and turnaround times, estimated from the flight list), the flight schedule, the navigation graph (a Gabriel graph on real waypoints or a rectangular grid of synthetic navpoints), the sector and capacity step, the trajectory generator (routed, time-stamped flight plans that keep every aircraft's legs in sequence inside the 24-hour window) and the solver transform. Each stage can be replaced by an own implementation through a common interface. A region is described by one configuration file (polygon, airports, time zone, time granularity, demand levels, seeds, capacities).

Further tools: 06_capacity_sweep.py computes each instance's nominal capacity and writes the capacity levels of 10 % to 100 % used in the published datasets; check_instances.py checks generated instances against the formal model (24-hour window, graph adjacency, aircraft rotations, sector cover); write_instance_info.py makes every instance self-describing; a regression harness checks that changes leave the output unchanged.

Compared with the first version, the demand model no longer discards the flights that cross UTC midnight, and destinations are drawn depending on origin and time of day. This version generated the V2 benchmark datasets: large-scaling 10.5281/zenodo.23039645 and small-scaling 10.5281/zenodo.23039835; the configurations that produced them ship with the datasets. The generator is described in the paper "An Open-Source Data Generator for Joint Air Traffic Flow and Capacity Management Benchmarking" (preprint: 10.5281/zenodo.23039874).

Requirements: Python 3.10 or later with pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, networkx and tqdm. Inputs: the OpenSky COVID-19 flight dataset (CC-BY-4.0), the OurAirports airport list (public domain, a snapshot is included) and, only for regions built on real waypoints, the X-Plane navigation data (GPL-2.0-or-later). The code is MIT licensed.
